title.value: Empirical Study on Optimizer Selection for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
title.justification: The paper is about examining the performance of various optimizers for out-of-distribution generalization.
title.quote: In this study, we examine the performance of popular first-order optimizers for different classes of distributional shift under empirical risk minimization and invariant risk minimization.

extractions.description: This study systematically evaluates the performance of popular adaptive and non-adaptive first-order optimizers in tasks involving out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in deep learning. It compares their effectiveness across various datasets and hyperparameter configurations, demonstrating that non-adaptive optimizers like momentum-based SGD often outperform adaptive ones like Adam in OOD settings. The research provides practitioners with insights into choosing optimizers for better OOD performance.

primary_category.justification: The paper mainly addresses the role of optimizers in out-of-distribution generalization within deep learning, a topic not directly related to eco-responsible AI categories such as climate change or sustainability.
primary_category.quote: Modern deep learning systems are fragile and do not generalize well under distribution shifts...a systematic study of the role of optimizers and their out-of-distribution generalization performance has not been undertaken.

secondary_categories.justification: Although not directly focused on climate applications, improvements in out-of-distribution generalization can enhance climate modeling and predictions by making models more robust to distributional shifts, which are prevalent in climate data.
secondary_categories.quote: In real-world applications, however, it is often the case that the test data obey a distribution different from the training data, and this distributional shift violates the typical independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumption.

primary_sub_category.justification: The specific focus of the paper on optimizer selection does not align with any of the eco-responsible sub-categories listed, which pertain to specific domains of climate change and sustainability.
primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we evaluate the OOD generalization performance on 10 typical OOD benchmarks using different optimizers.

applications.value: Improved robustness in deep learning models to distributional shifts
applications.justification: The paper's insights on optimizer selection can apply to making AI models more robust in various real-world tasks, including those related to climate science.
applications.quote: We search over a wide range of hyperparameters and examine the classification accuracy (in-distribution and out-of-distribution) for over 20,000 models. These findings can help practitioners choose the right optimizer and know what behavior to expect.
